comments.post_content: DoorDash Driver Highlights Impact of Trump's 'No Tax on Tips' Policy After White House Delivery A DoorDash driver who recently delivered a McDonald's order to the White House says she has personally benefited from President Donald Trump's "no tax on tips" policy included in his broader tax and border legislation. Sharron Simmons, who said she has been delivering with DoorDash since 2022, described the experience as both historic and financially meaningful after becoming the first DoorDash driver to deliver a meal to the White House. Simmons said the tax policy has increased her take-home income and estimated she could save between $3,000 and $4,000 under the current rules. The measure is part of Trump's "One Big Beautiful Bill," a legislative package that includes tax relief for tipped workers, temporary elimination of taxes on overtime pay, and an increase in the child tax credit. Supporters argue the policy helps workers keep more of their earnings and stimulates economic activity. Critics, however, warn that the tax cuts could reduce government revenue and add pressure to the federal deficit. Simmons said she hopes the no-tax-on-tips provision will continue beyond its current expiration date in 2028 but added she plans to benefit from the policy while it remains in place. Universal Coverage: All residents are entitled to basic healthcare through one of four nonprofit health plans.

The delivery, handled by Arkansas grandmother Sharon Simmons, served as a live-action testimonial for the 2025 "One Big Beautiful Bill," which Simmons credited with saving her $11,000 in tax-free gratuities over the last year. Between bags of burgers, Trump leaned into the spectacle, jokingly asking reporters, "This doesn't look staged, does it?" before peeling off a $100 bill for Simmons as a personal tip. #Trump #NoTaxOnTips #DoorDash #OvalOffice #OneBigBeautifulBill

The delivery, handled by Arkansas grandmother Sharon Simmons, served as a live-action testimonial for the 2025 "One Big Beautiful Bill," which Simmons credited with saving her $11,000 in tax-free gratuities over the last year. Between bags of burgers, Trump leaned into the spectacle, jokingly asking reporters, "This doesn't look staged, does it?" before peeling off a $100 bill for Simmons as a personal tip. #Trump #NoTaxOnTips #DoorDash #OvalOffice #OneBigBeautifulBill

Between bags of burgers, Trump leaned into the spectacle, jokingly asking reporters, "This doesn't look staged, does it?" before peeling off a $100 bill for Simmons as a personal tip. #Trump #NoTaxOnTips #DoorDash #OvalOffice #OneBigBeautifulBill

comments.post_content: Congress just gave tipped workers a new tax deduction worth up to $25,000. And in the same breath, kept the federal tipped minimum wage at $2.13/hr — where it's been since 1991. A tax break on poverty wages is still poverty wages. Workers deserve both: the deduction and a base wage they can actually live on. If you earn tips in food, hospitality, or beauty services, claim what you're owed this tax season. Then help us fight for the raise that no tax code can replace. #OneFairWage #NoTaxOnTips #TippedWorkers #taxday
